hook: Andrej Karpathy has spent his career moving between building frontier neural networks and teaching other people how they work. He was a founding research scientist at OpenAI in 2015, then spent five years as Tesla's Director of AI leading the computer vision team behind Autopilot and Full Self-Driving. Along the way he designed and taught CS231n, Stanford's first deep learning course, and built a large public following through blog posts and YouTube lectures that walk through how language models are actually built. After a second stint at OpenAI and a run at his own AI education venture, Eureka Labs, he joined Anthropic's pretraining team in May 2026.

standing.watch: What remains unresolved in the records is the legal activity around the companies he is tied to. The lawsuits naming OpenAI and Anthropic are all recorded as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker, so no outcome or next step is shown. The most recent item naming Karpathy is the October 2026 story about his shift from coding to directing AI agents, which follows his May 2026 move to Anthropic's pretraining team. The records do not show a pending case against him personally, a planned listing, or a dispute in which he is a named party. Where the records are thin, they say less: there is no further detail on Eureka Labs beyond its founding in 2024, and no valuation or funding figures for OpenAI or Tesla.

OpenAI appears as a company he founded, and Tesla appears as a company where he is an executive. The lawsuits on the site include Bass v. OpenAI, United States v. OpenAI OpCo, Buist v. Anthropic, Jiang v. OpenAI Group, Grant v. OpenAI Inc., Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, and The Seattle Times Company v. OpenAI Inc., all marked as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. The pattern running through the record is that his profile is built from his roles at OpenAI, Tesla, Eureka Labs and now Anthropic, while the legal coverage clusters around OpenAI and, in one instance, Anthropic, the two labs where he has worked. The single news story naming him, from October 2026, describes a shift in focus from coding to directing AI agents.
standing.standing: Andrej Karpathy stands as a researcher who has moved between the largest labs and a public teaching role, and the records place him at Anthropic's pretraining team as of May 2026. He is listed as a founder of OpenAI, where he was a founding research scientist in 2015, and as an executive of Tesla, where he was Director of AI from 2017 to 2022 leading the computer vision team for Autopilot and Full Self-Driving. He also returned to OpenAI from 2023 to 2024 to build a team focused on midtraining and synthetic data generation, and he founded the AI education venture Eureka Labs in 2024. His influence in the records rests on that mix of frontier lab work and public explanation, including CS231n at Stanford and a large following through blog posts and YouTube lectures.
